thesis_title: Farmulate: Optimizing Crop Rotation and Companion Planting Through XGBoost and YOLOv8n Algorithms Based on Soil Analysis
description: This study addresses the lack of simple and accessible tools for soil analysis, crop rotation, and companion planting, especially for small-scale and beginner farmers. Titled “Farmulate: Optimizing Crop Rotation and Companion Planting Through Machine Learning and Image Processing Algorithms Based on Soil Analysis,” it aims to help users choose suitable crops and planting strategies using machine learning and image processing. Designed for farmers, agricultural practitioners, and learners, the system analyzes soil images and sensor-based nutrient data to identify soil type and recommend appropriate crops and companion plants. It is expected to improve soil health, increase crop yield, and reduce the need for expensive laboratory soil testing, contributing to more sustainable and data-driven farming practices.

thesis_title: A Machine Learning Approach to Parking Systems with Bidirectional Search and A* Algorithm for Optimized Pathfinding
description: This study addresses the problem of inefficient parking search and route navigation in urban environments with limited real-time parking data. Titled “A Machine Learning Approach to Parking Systems with Bidirectional Search and A Algorithms for Optimized Pathfinding,”* it aims to recommend suitable parking areas and generate efficient routes using machine learning–based suitability ranking and graph-based pathfinding algorithms. Designed for urban drivers and parking system administrators, the system evaluates parking options based on distance, cost, safety, accessibility, and operating hours, while computing optimal routes using Bidirectional A*. It is expected to reduce parking search time, traffic congestion, and user decision effort, contributing to smarter, more sustainable urban mobility solutions.

thesis_title: Smart Recommendation System for Electric Consumption on Appliance-Level Data With an Arduino-Based Device for Data Gathering Using LSTM Forecasting Algorithm
description: The study addresses the need for appliance‑level energy monitoring to help users reduce unnecessary electricity consumption through third-party devices. The research “Smart Recommendation System for Electric Consumption on Appliance-Level Data With an Arduino-Based Device for Data Gathering Using LSTM Forecasting Algorithm” aims to forecast electric usage through LSTM algorithm and use it together with historical data through an Arduino-based device to provide energy‑saving suggestions with a recommendation system. Intended for households that uses electricity especially individuals seeking to monitor and optimize their energy use. Through data‑driven insights, the project contributes to sustainable energy management by offering a low‑cost, intelligent solution for appliance‑level monitoring and optimization.

thesis_title: REFocus:Screen-Locking Android Application Using Decision Tree for Managing Screen-Time Overuse
description: This study addresses of overuse of screentime. Titled “ReFocus”, it aims to Lessen Screentime USe using Decision Tree and Locking Mechanisms. Designed to limit screentime overuse for android users, the system Records screentime and decides if the user overuse it. It is expected to Lock app specified by the user, contributing to Lessen Screentime and improve general focus and productivity.

thesis_title: Sentiment Analysis of Structured and Unstructured Employee Feedback in a Multi-Tenant Environment Using Machine Learning Algorithms.
description: This study addresses the difficulty in manually analyzing and quantifying large volumes of qualitative employee feedback to extract actionable organizational insights. Titled "Kobo Sentiment Analyzer", it aims to automate the evaluation of employee satisfaction and identifying key themes in questionnaire responses using Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques including VADER for sentiment analysis and BERTopic for topic modeling. Designed for Human Resources (HR) departments and organizational managers, the system processes text-based feedback to visualize sentiment trends, correlations, and feature importance. It is expected to provide real-time, objective insights into workforce morale, contributing to data-driven decision-making for improving organizational culture and employee retention.

thesis_title: Using Logistic Regression to Predict Popular Products from Historical Sales Data at OBM Furniture
description: This study addresses the problem of manual sales record-keeping and limited data-driven decision-making at OBM Furniture. Titled “Using Logistic Regression to Predict Popular Products from Historical Sales Data at OBM Furniture”, it aims to develop a web-based data analytics and predictive system that digitizes sales records, analyzes sales trends, and predicts popular products based on historical data. The system processes sales transactions and applies logistic regression to classify and forecast product demand. It is expected to provide a decision-support dashboard that presents summarized reports, trends, and predictive results, contributing to improved inventory planning, marketing strategies, and overall business decision-making.

thesis_title: Automated Python Codebase Documentation Generation Using Abstract Syntax Trees And Natural Language Processing
category: Natural Language Processing & Large Language Model
description: This study addresses the persistent challenge of manual documentation in software development by developing an automated system that leverages Abstract Syntax Trees (AST) for structural code parsing and Natural Language Processing (NLP) for semantic description generation. By integrating these technologies, the research provides a highly acceptable solution that improves documentation efficiency and accuracy, bridging the gap between raw Python source code and comprehensive technical manuals.

thesis_title: Cleft2Speech: Phoneme-Level Speech Correction in Post-Cleft Palate Rehabilitation: Integrating Automatic Speech Recognition and Cloning Speech Synthesis
description: This study addresses the significant speech articulation difficulties post-cleft surgery and the lack of personalized, real-time therapy. Titled “CLEFT2SPEECH: Phoneme-Level Speech Correction in Post-Cleft Palate Rehabilitation”, it aims to develop a web-based articulation correction system for patients using Transducer-ASR, Phoneme Mapping, and voice cloning technologies. Designed for patients and Speech-Language Pathologists (SLPs), the system processes speech, identifies misarticulated phonemes, and generates an intelligible, corrected audio sample in the patient's voice. It is expected to enhance speech clarity and provide real-time articulation modeling, contributing to better communication outcomes and expanding therapy access in underserved regions.

thesis_title: Utilizing Optical Character Recognition and Natural Language Processing for Automated Digital Medical Term Flashcards within a Web-Based Platform
category: Large Language Model & Natural Language Processing
description: This study addresses the challenge of producing structured flashcards from medical-related text. Titled “Utilizing Optical Character Recognition and Natural Language Processing for Automated Digital Medical Term Flashcards within a Web-Based Platform,” it aims to assist pre-medical students in creating digital flashcards from medical learning materials using a language model and OCR for text extraction. The system accepts inputs in forms of images of text, plain text, Word, PDFs, and PowerPoint files, and generates formatted digital flashcards. It is expected to advance understanding of the viability of smaller models, demonstrating that very large models are not required for specific tasks, thereby contributing to research on the accessibility of language models.

thesis_title: OptiPack: LiDAR-Enhanced Measurement of Items with Dynamic Programming using Constraint Satisfaction Problems for the Optimization of Travel and Logistics Packaging
description: This study addresses the inefficiencies and guesswork involved in traditional packing methods, particularly in small-scale shipping, travel, and logistics scenarios. Titled “OptiPack: A LiDAR-Powered Packing Optimization Application Using 3D Scanning and Dynamic Programming,” it aims to improve packing accuracy and space utilization through advanced 3D scanning and optimization techniques. Designed for consumers and small logistics providers, the system uses LiDAR sensors on iPhone models 12 Pro and above to generate precise 3D object models and simulate their arrangement within containers. By applying a dynamic programming–based optimization algorithm, OptiPack suggests efficient packing configurations, reducing wasted space and packing time. The system is expected to enhance resource management, improve loading efficiency, and contribute to more streamlined and stress-free packing processes.

thesis_title: INET: Identifying Networks of Elevated Temperatures for Urban Heat Island Hotspot Detection in Valenzuela City Using Satellite Imagery
description: This study addresses the hotspots or areas where heat is highly indicated around Valenzuela. Titled “INET: Identifying Networks of Elevated Temperatures for Urban Heat Island Hotspot Detection in Valenzuela City Using Satellite Imagery”, it aims to identify places of elevated temperatures in Valenzuela using satellite imagery. Designed for local government units (LGUs), urban planners, GIS analysts, and environmental officers, the system serves as a web-based visualization platform that integrates externally processed satellite-derived land surface temperature and spatial clustering results to detect and display urban heat island hotspots. It is expected to enhance localized urban heat monitoring and support data-driven planning and mitigation strategies, contributing to climate-resilient, sustainable urban development and evidence-based decision-making in Valenzuela City.

thesis_title: CritiCheck: An Intelligent Tutoring System for Auto-Grading Python Code Using LoRA and QLoRA-Finetuned Language Models
description: This study addresses the need for an intelligent system that can auto grade Python code submissions efficiently and provide constructive feedback for improvement. Titled “CritiCheck: An Intelligent Tutoring System for Auto-Grading Python Code Using LoRA and QLoRA-Finetuned Language Models,” it aims to automate the evaluation of Python code submissions, integrating both rule-based and AI-driven evaluation mechanisms using LoRA and QLoRA fine-tuned models. Designed for educational institutions, software engineering programs, and online learning platforms, the system evaluates the logic, output, style, and other quality characteristics of Python code. It is expected to streamline the grading process, provide actionable feedback to learners, and enhance the learning experience. This contributes to the improvement of educational tools by utilizing AI to support efficient and objective grading, ensuring high-quality student engagement and outcomes.

thesis_title: SmartMinutes: An English-Tagalog Voice and Audio-Driven System using Natural Language Processing for Automated Meeting Transcription and Customizable Minute Templates
category: Natural Language Processing & Large Language Model

thesis_title: Caniscan: Dog skin disease detection and diagnosing program using YOLOv8 and Llama 3.2 treatment-based recommendation
description: This study addresses the lack of systematic canine skin disease diagnosis in veterinary clinics due to limited manpower and time-consuming manual inspection. Titled "Caniscan: Dog Skin Disease Detection and Diagnosing Program Using YOLOv8 and Llama 3.2 Treatment-Based Recommendation", it aims to develop an automated diagnostic support system using YOLOv8 for real-time disease detection and Llama 3.2 for treatment recommendations. Designed for veterinarians, veterinary clinics, and pet owners, the system analyzes dog skin images to detect and classify four common conditions (allergic dermatitis, fungal infection, hot spots, and mange) with confidence-level predictions and AI-generated treatment guidance.

thesis_title: ANA: A Smart Noise Pollution Index (NPI) Mapping System Using Digital Signal Processing (DSP) Technique and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs)
Optimizing Workforce Efficiency in Construction Companies Using Intelligent Job Matching System
description: This study addresses inefficiencies in workforce allocation within construction companies, particularly the mismatch between worker skills and assigned tasks that leads to productivity loss and project delays. Titled “Optimizing Workforce Efficiency in Construction Companies Using an Intelligent Job Matching System,” it aims to optimize workforce deployment using a hybrid recommendation approach that integrates user profiling, content-based filtering, and collaborative filtering techniques. Designed for construction companies and project managers, the system automates job–worker matching based on skill compatibility and historical performance. It is expected to improve workforce utilization, reduce trade stacking, and minimize project delays, contributing to enhanced productivity and more efficient workforce management.

thesis_title: Wingpedia:  Identifying Bird Species with a Bird Watching Assistance Application with Image Recognition using YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once) and Audio Recognition using Convolutional Neural Networks.
description: The study addresses the difficulties people have during birdwatching such as locating and identifying bird species. Titled "Wingpedia", it aims to create an android application that is able to assist and be accessible to a diverse range of users, utilize models such as YOLOv8 and CNNs, and examine its effectiveness. Designed for birdwatchers, the system identifies bird species using YOLOv8 image identification or CNNs audio recognition technology. It is expected to identify the species of the targeted contributing to enhance the birdwatching experience as well as to raise awareness and appreciation towards bird species in the country.

thesis_title: DocuTrack: A Hybrid Cryptographically Secured Web-Based Framework for Academic Document Submission and Verification Using AES,RSA, and SHA-256
mentor: Ms. May Florence D. San Pablo
description: This study addresses the problem of academic document tampering, unauthorized modification, and difficulty in verifying the authenticity of submitted assignments in digital submission environments. Titled “DocuTrack: A Web-Based Secure Academic Document Submission and Verification System using AES, RSA, and SHA-256”, it aims to develop a secure system that ensures the authenticity, integrity, and originality of academic documents using cryptographic techniques such as AES encryption, RSA digital signatures, and SHA-256 hashing. Designed for academic institutions, instructors, and students, the system securely issues personalized documents, verifies immutable signed headers, and detects tampering or duplication through answer-only hashing. It is expected to strengthen trust in digital academic submissions, reduce plagiarism and forgery, and contribute to improved security and reliability in academic document management systems.

thesis_title: CryptoGauge: Cryptocurrency Price Trend Prediction Using Sentiment Analysis with Real Time Data Scraping
description: This study addresses the lack of guidance and decision support for beginner cryptocurrency traders, which often leads to impulsive and uninformed trading. Titled “CRYPTOGAUGE: A Decision Support System for Beginner Cryptocurrency Traders Using Sentiment Analysis and Topic Modeling”, it aims to improve trading confidence and decision-making using machine learning-based sentiment analysis, topic modeling, and data processing techniques. Designed for beginner cryptocurrency traders, the system analyzes real-time market-related data to provide intelligent insights and guidance. It is expected to enhance financial literacy, promote responsible trading behavior, and support digital financial innovation, contributing to SDG 4 (Quality Education), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), and SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure).
